method: Claims extracted from 7 comparison/porting docs across llm-relay and freellmapi, then adversarially verified against source. TRUE requires a path:line anchor.

verdicts.claim: LLM-based tool-argument repair (a reshaper model) was deliberately NOT proposed to freellmapi — freellmapi's deterministic double-encoding repair (#794), Ajv verdict (#802) and large failover pool are cheaper, faster, and cannot hallucinate an argument
verdicts.evidence: Doc lists it first under "Considered and not recommended" (freellmapi-gap-proposals-2026-08-10.md:166-169). llm-relay does own the reshaper it declined to propose: src/reshaper.ts (HttpReshaper/FailoverReshaper) driven from src/repair.ts:96. freellmapi has no counterpart — `grep -rli reshaper C:\Code\freellmapi\server\src` returns nothing — while both cited replacements exist: server/src/lib/tool-args.ts (merged 8f99a2b, #794, 2026-08-10) and server/src/lib/tool-validate.ts (0ed6dba, #802, same day). The comparative judgment ("cheaper, faster, cannot hallucinate") is an opinion, but each factual premise it rests on holds.

verdicts.claim: Locally-synced benchmark/capability ranking with provenance (BFCL, LMArena, Aider merged) was NOT proposed — it duplicates the signed catalog's intelligence_rank/speed_rank with more moving parts and no signature
verdicts.evidence: Listed as not-recommended at freellmapi-gap-proposals-2026-08-10.md:170-172, and no §2 proposal covers it. llm-relay's version is real and unsigned: scripts/sync-tiers.mjs:37-43 fetches OpenRouter/BFCL/LMArena/Aider/ArtificialAnalysis into docs/tier-data.json, consumed by src/benchmarks.ts:196 (deploymentFitness) with no signature check. freellmapi's catalog carries both columns (server/src/db/migrations/20260101_000000_legacy_baseline.ts:65-66). ⚠ Reason is now half-stale: freellmapi derives SPEED locally (services/scoring.ts:157 observedSpeedRank), so only intelligence_rank is purely catalog-sourced — the same narrowing PORTING item 5 records.

verdicts.claim: llm-relay's per-install capability-token control plane (src/control-authorization.ts) was NOT proposed — freellmapi's session auth on /api/* plus the unified key on /v1/* is a coherent and adequate model, no gap
verdicts.evidence: freellmapi-gap-proposals-2026-08-10.md:173-175 lists it as not-recommended. The llm-relay mechanism exists as described (src/control-authorization.ts:28-29 FILE_MODE 0600/0700, timing-safe compare, per-install token). freellmapi's stated model is real: server/src/middleware/requireAuth.ts:7 ("/v1 surface authenticates with the unified API key"), server/src/routes/anthropic.ts:196-197 timing-safe unified-key check, server/src/middleware/rateLimit.ts:5.

verdicts.claim: Loopback-only enforcement was NOT proposed — llm-relay refused to bind non-loopback by design while freellmapi is deliberately deployable (HOST/HOST_BIND, Desktop LAN toggle); a different product, not a gap
verdicts.evidence: Not-recommended entry at freellmapi-gap-proposals-2026-08-10.md:176-177. llm-relay enforces it in config load: src/config.ts:841-846 throws "config.listen must bind loopback … Refusing to expose a keyed, unauthenticated proxy on a non-loopback address." freellmapi defaults to a public bind: server/src/lib/config.ts:66 `host: process.env.HOST ?? '::'`, with its own test setting HOST=0.0.0.0 (server/src/__tests__/lib/config.test.ts:24).

verdicts.claim: The dispatch ladder / peer-CLI lanes / lane discovery (src/dispatch.ts, src/lane-probe.ts) were NOT proposed — they render shell commands for other vendors' CLIs and are not proxy features
verdicts.evidence: freellmapi-gap-proposals-2026-08-10.md:178-179 lists them as out of scope, and no §2/§4 item proposes them. Both named files exist in llm-relay (src/dispatch.ts, src/lane-probe.ts, plus src/lane-manifest.ts), and the reason still holds in code: the relay only renders commands — CLAUDE.md's "relay never spawns a cli rung" is borne out by /dispatch living in src/routes/admin.ts:210 as a data endpoint with no child-process spawn on the request path.

verdicts.claim: The Anthropic passthrough / subagent-offload lane (lib/anthropic-passthrough.ts, lib/subagent-detect.ts) is deliberately excluded from proposals — a standing local-only decision kept on feat/anthropic-passthrough and never to be sent upstream
verdicts.evidence: Stated at freellmapi-gap-proposals-2026-08-10.md:198-203 and confirmed by the trees: `git ls-tree feat/anthropic-passthrough server/src/lib/` lists anthropic-passthrough.ts and subagent-detect.ts, while the same listing against origin/main returns neither, and C:\Code\freellmapi (main @ 0a8a3f7) has no such files. The live tree C:\Users\ethan\freellmapi\app is checked out on feat/anthropic-passthrough and does carry both.

verdicts.claim: As of 2026-08-14 every adopted item in §1 and §2 is implemented with pinning tests, the deferred-commit machinery withholds both fronts until meaningful content (including empty-stream and unparseable-dialect failover), and the OpenAI direct-path dialect gap recorded as coverage item 2 in tool-call-dialect-leak.md is closed
verdicts.evidence: All twelve §1 items and all twelve §2 adopted items resolve to code plus a test (itemized in the per-item verdicts below); even the manifest-only item is pinned — test/server-safety.test.ts:138 asserts engines.node === ">=22". Deferred commit runs on BOTH fronts through one module: src/stream-commit.ts:255 probeStreamForCommit, called at src/server.ts:736 (anthropic-messages) and src/server.ts:1866-1868 (openai-chat/openai-responses), with headers written only after commit (src/server.ts:818-822) and dead pre-commit probes continuing the walk (src/server.ts:754-760, 1888-1897). Empty stream: src/stream-commit.ts:143-145,192,222-224 "stream completed without meaningful content" → dead, pinned by test/deferred-commit.test.ts:278. Unparseable dialect: test/openai-dialect-passthrough.test.ts:334 (pre-commit failover) vs :392 (post-commit honest mid-stream error). Coverage item 2 is marked closed at docs/tool-call-dialect-leak.md:122-129 and backed by src/openai-dialect.ts + test/openai-dialect-passthrough.test.ts. §2.7 and §2.12 remain genuinely absent.

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED: deferred stream commit point — withhold the response skeleton until first meaningful content so connect errors, in-band error frames, empty completions and unparseable dialect turns fail over with zero bytes on the wire
verdicts.evidence: src/stream-commit.ts holds raw bytes until the client-facing protocol carries text/reasoning/a structured tool call (anthropicVerdict :63-105, openAiChatVerdict :114-146, openAiResponsesVerdict :161-204), replaying the prefix byte-exact (:281-304) inside a 64 KiB bound (:27,323). In-band error frames are dead pre-commit (:65-67,115-117,163-165,219-221,235-237) — closing the exact `invalidEnvelopeReason` hole the review named. Wired at src/server.ts:736 and :1868; headers deferred to src/server.ts:818-822 and :1940-1947. Tests: test/stream-commit.test.ts, test/deferred-commit.test.ts:252-448. The freellmapi citations check out at the exact lines given: routes/proxy.ts:2051-2060 is the `!headerSent` licence-to-throw, proxy.ts:2006 is the 256-char dialect probe, lib/inbound-chat.ts:332+ holds `committed`/`heldText`.

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED: split the streaming deadline into a first-byte grace plus an inter-byte stall watchdog
verdicts.evidence: src/config.ts:87-93,519-520,1051-1052 add per-provider `stallTimeoutMs`; src/server.ts:1102-1129 `withStallWatchdog` re-arms per chunk through the same AbortController, DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000 (:1104). Both fronts disarm the total deadline and hand over at commit: src/server.ts:788-791 and :1927-1930, with `stallTimeoutMs: 0` preserving the old single deadline. Test: test/mid-stream-failure.test.ts:244-345 (stalling vs slow-but-alive backends, and the 0 case). Note on wording: the pre-commit window is the existing per-attempt `timeoutMs`, not a separately derived grace, and the handover point is first *meaningful content* rather than first byte — which is exactly what §1.2's own prescription asked for.

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED: process-level transport-error safety net — uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers with a pure classifier walking the error cause chain, swallowing only a closed allowlist of undici/socket reset codes
verdicts.evidence: src/process-safety-net.ts:20-38 closed code allowlist (ECONNRESET…UND_ERR_ABORTED), :43-50 a short Node/undici message-shape list, :52-60 a bounded cycle-safe `walkErrorChain` over `err.cause`; installed once at startup from src/cli.ts:559 `installProcessSafetyNet`. Test: test/pool-failover.test.ts:703 ("an attempt in flight is never aborted", ≥2 candidates).

verdicts.evidence: src/server.ts:1147-1152 `dropRemainingSameProvider`, called from exactly the two transport catch blocks and only when the abort was not this relay's own deadline: src/server.ts:684 (`if (!aborted)`, Anthropic front) and src/server.ts:1812 (OpenAI front). It composes with the existing stop_reason pre-pass (:83-95), i.e. a second rung in an existing slot exactly as claimed. Test: test/repair.test.ts:294.

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED: the ASCII `<|tool_call_begin|>` Kimi/DeepSeek dialect marker variant

Test: test/tool-dialects.test.ts:89 ("kimi ASCII token dialect (adoption review §1.8)"). freellmapi's side is confirmed at server/src/lib/tool-call-rescue.ts:47-51, where the same ASCII markers head its DIALECT_MARKERS array.

verdicts.evidence: llm-relay stores one scalar on existing breaker state — src/circuit-breaker.ts:26,55,74 declare `quotaPercent?: number | null` and :412 assigns it; there is no observations table, no confidence ranking, and no persistence beyond the breaker's in-memory state. No SQLite dependency exists (package.json:44-47 lists only ajv and llm-bridge).

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED: windowed freshness in the real-world score — score from the 50-call recentCalls window llm-relay already records

verdicts.claim: SKIPPED: freellmapi's writeback half (periodically rewriting catalog speed_rank from observations) — 'capability data is synced, never typed'
verdicts.evidence: Nothing under src/ writes docs/tier-data.json: src/tier-data.ts and src/benchmarks.ts contain no writeFileSync, and the only writer in the repo is scripts/sync-tiers.mjs. verdicts.evidence: src/catalog.ts:14-16 defines MAX_CATALOG_BYTES (2MB), MAX_CATALOG_MODELS (5000) and MAX_MODEL_ID_CHARS (256); :20 refuses a stated oversize from `content-length` before reading; :387 streams through `readBoundedBody`; :390-394 truncates a pathological model count with a warning; :398,404 drop over-long ids. verdicts.evidence: src/catalog.ts:388 reads exactly one envelope key — `JSON.parse(body) as { data?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }` — with no alias walk. No price-magnitude inference exists: the only scaling is the deterministic unit conversion src/metadata.ts:27-30 (`perToken * 1e6`), which guesses nothing about a published figure's magnitude.

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED: an unrepairable schema-invalid tool call becomes a dead turn that resumes the candidate walk — failover AFTER repair fails, buffered path only BY DESIGN
verdicts.evidence: src/server.ts:824-833: when `repairPath` reports exhaustion the walk records a dead turn (`pool429.recordDeadTurn()`), drops duplicate entries for the same deployment, and `continue`s to the next candidate; only with nowhere left to go does it fail 502 (:836-862). Repair still runs first, so the contract order is repair→failover. Buffered-only is structural, not an omission: headers are committed at src/server.ts:818-822 before `repairPath` for a streamed response, and the commit boundary treats a structured tool_use start as meaningful content (src/stream-commit.ts:77-79). The outcome is a first-class log status (src/log.ts:7,111; src/server.ts:2507). Test: test/pool-failover.test.ts:794.

verdicts.claim: ADOPTED with guardrails: sticky-session affinity — 30-min pin keyed on a session header or first-user-message hash, with a provenance header, always losing to breaker/health ordering, and NO response-body retention
verdicts.evidence: src/session-pin.ts:21-22 (30-min sliding TTL, 1000-entry LRU), :89-98 keys on the relay-owned `x-llm-relay-session` or a 16-hex SHA-256 of the first user message, compounded by the documented agent id only. Pins hold `targetSpec` and timestamps — no bodies (:9-14). Guardrails in src/server.ts:962-989: a pin that is cooling, credential-faulted, absent from the pool, or in the degrade tail while a live in-band member exists is bypassed with a reason; provenance rides `x-llm-relay-sticky` (:1002-1006, header name at src/session-pin.ts:4); pins are created only after a successful multi-candidate route (:1008-1016). Off by default (src/server.ts:220-222). Tests: test/sticky-sessions.test.ts:184-441, test/session-pin.test.ts.

verdicts.evidence: llm-relay's pin record is `{ targetSpec, pinnedAt, lastUsedAt, useCount }` (src/session-pin.ts:9-14) — no content field exists. freellmapi does keep the trace: server/src/routes/proxy.ts:162 `const reasoningMemory = new Map<string, { reasoning: string; modelKey: string; lastUsed: number }>()` with :173-175 `rememberReasoning`, alongside its own stickySessionMap at :150-151. Its sticky key also accepts a client `sessionIdHeader` (routes/proxy.ts:245), which llm-relay deliberately does not (test/sticky-sessions.test.ts:395).
